name: GRMZK-1
description: Discovered in July 2025 on the left bank of the Daugava. Five metres, about three tonnes, hull intact. Origin and classification remain unknown. Under observation by the research group.

name: Local Nomad
where: In front of the Jyväskylä Art Museum, Kauppakatu 23
author: Jukka Silokunnas, Jonna Surhasko
description: A rag-boiling sphere from the rag house of the old Kangas paper mill. Every year it gets a new colour (purple in 2026) and stands in front of the art museum from summer until the first snow. According to the museum, the sphere travels the world and always comes back.

name: Silo 468
author: Lighting Design Collective
description: A 1960s oil silo for 16,000 m³. Since 2012 it has been a light installation and a public space: 1,280 LEDs shine through holes cut in its wall, in patterns driven by the wind. The inner walls are dark red.

name: Fröndenberg Funnel
author: Markus Lüpertz
description: A fibre-catching funnel that cleaned the water of the Himmelmann paper mill and returned the fibre to production from 1959 to 1982. Townspeople and the painter Markus Lüpertz saved it, and in 1998 he painted it. Now an industrial monument.

name: Ladle of Steel
author: Steve Tomlinson
description: A real ladle from a local foundry. Since 2005 it has hung above a roundabout, pouring steel into a mould.

name: Waypoint (the Acid Ball)
author: Mutuus Studio
description: A 1938 sphere from the pressure-relief system of the Georgia-Pacific pulp mill, where wood chips were cooked in sulphurous acid. Since 2018 it has been covered in reflective glass beads and lit with LEDs. At night you can light it up with your own torch.

name: Eco Earth
author: Idea of former mayor Roger Gertenrich
description: An acid tank from a paper mill. In 2003 it was covered in tiles and turned into a globe. The tiles are slowly falling off.

name: The Savannah Globe
where: Corner of White Bluff Rd and DeRenne Ave
author: James Ellison, Leo Berkemeier (first painting)
description: A Horton sphere built in 1956–57 for the Savannah Gas Company to hold 600,000 cubic feet of gas. It stopped holding gas in the 1970s. From the start it was painted as the Earth with a single word: SAVANNAH. The new owners of the site are keeping it as a landmark open to everyone.

name: The Tank with the Crank
author: Dave Pahl
description: A rusty water tank from the fort's barracks, turned into a kinetic sculpture. Gears from an old cement mixer sit inside and a crank sticks out. Turn it, and a whale and a fisherman in a boat circle above the tank.

name: Rusty the Mastodon
where: Opposite the Pritzlaff Building, 150 W. St. Paul Ave.
author: Kendall Breunig
description: An old steel boiler from the Nunn-Bush shoe factory, made into Rusty the mastodon.

name: The Way
author: Alexander Liberman
description: Decommissioned steel tanks, already 40–50 years old when the sculptor got them in 1980, cut and assembled into a monumental sculpture. Recently restored, the tanks are now about a hundred years old.

name: Nikotan's Gas Sphere
author: Shibata Gas
description: A gas sphere still in service. Many Japanese gas companies paint their spheres; on this one the character Nikotan smiles at the town. Its face outweighs its working life.

name: Immerge
author: Chris Fox
description: A public installation made from the parts of the water tank of the former Rozelle tram depot. Opened in April 2022.

name: Martin Luther
where: Small museum at the town entrance
description: A McLaren steam traction engine built in Leeds in 1895. Brought in 1896 to haul cargo across the Namib desert, it got stuck in the sand for good, hence its name: “Here I stand”. Restored from rusty scrap in 1973, it now stands under the glass shell of a small museum.

name: Home. Memories
author: balbek bureau, Wonder Workshop
description: The station's old fuel tank, no longer in use. Since February 2023 a thin metal frame of a Ukrainian house, like a pencil drawing, stands around it. About 4,000 visitors a year see it first.

name: Nomad's Twin
description: The second sphere from the same Kangas rag house, kept on the former mill site as a monument. Exact spot and condition not yet checked.

name: Kugelkocher
description: A rag-boiling sphere, later used to soak waste paper for cardboard. Made in 1913 by Ernst Zorn in Regensburg. In 1926 a wall was taken down to bring it into the mill, where it still stands.

name: The Canton Acid Ball
where: Site of the demolished paper mill
description: A riveted 1936 sphere that held alum under pressure, possibly made at the mill itself. Found during the demolition of the paper mill in October 2026. Its fate is undecided; one idea is to place it by the future riverfront.

name: Gas Works Park
author: Richard Haag (park)
description: A coal gasification plant that worked from 1906 to 1956. Richard Haag's park, opened in 1975, left its towers standing as they were; locals call them Seattle's iron Stonehenge. The last remains of a coal gas plant in the US, on the National Register since 2013.

name: Worried Buoy
author: Unknown
description: An old buoy painted as a pot-bellied little man with a worried face.

name: Robot Cisterns
author: Clark Ellefson (Lewis + Clark), Chris Stuyck (Stuyck Company)
description: Two decommissioned propane tanks turned into robots that work as rainwater cisterns. Installed on 9 April 2018.

name: Big Rig Jig
author: Mike Ross
description: Two tanker trucks, bent and stacked into a curving tower.

name: Future Returns
where: Shown at 20-21 Arts Centre; current location unknown
author: Dan Rawlings
description: An oil tanker that stood idle for 12 years. The artist plasma-cut its walls into a forest.

name: Moby Train
where: Van Praet roundabout near Train World
author: François Schuiten, Pierre Matter
description: Locomotive 5204 “Gros Nez” from 1957, placed inside the sculpture of a whale. Planned for the roundabout by the railway museum; not installed before 2029.

name: Mushrooms and Bird Blind
author: Abe Singer
description: The sculptor cut an old water tank the size of a boxcar into mushrooms and a blind for watching birds.

name: Boston Buoy Trail
author: Carrie Reichardt (mosaics)
description: Century-old sea buoys covered in mosaic and placed around the town by the Transported programme.

name: Frampton Marsh Buoys
author: Nathan Murdoch, Adam O'Brien
description: Former sea buoys turned into an artwork in a bird reserve.

name: Lakes Entrance Buoys
author: Lukas Kasper
description: Huge old buoys painted by the artist.

name: Woolgoolga Buoys
where: Corner of Wharf St and Beach St
author: Sev Appleton
description: Old buoys that have stood as a town sculpture since 2000.

name: Buoy in a Field
author: Unknown
description: A retired light buoy standing in the middle of a field, far from the sea.

name: The Bathysphere
where: New York Aquarium, Coney Island, left of the main entrance
description: A cast steel sphere with portholes that set records for deep-sea dives. It has stood at the aquarium entrance since 1957.

name: Mantis Dreaming
author: Bill Secunda
description: A praying mantis made mostly from a scrapped railway tank car.

name: Stork's Nest
author: Idea by Stina, age five; creative lead Kristel Linnutaja
description: An old lighting mast of the port area now carries a light installation: a stork's nest with eggs. A five-year-old girl drew the idea.

name: Tin Man
description: A rooftop water tank styled as the Tin Man, with murals on the wall below.

name: Sky Chair
author: Villu Jaanisoo
description: A giant seat assembled from blue metal barrels, standing in a meadow of the art park. Its blue argues with the earth and grass and echoes the sky.
